newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bank shares recover, future seen brighter. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank shares recover, future seen brighter. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Switzerland's two biggest banks rallied as investors recovered from disappointment that Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) and CS Holding had not sold large utility holdings.

As the shares recuperated on Tuesday , analysts said all three major Swiss banks -- UBS, CS Holding and Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) -- were now well placed to improve profitibility after a recent round of extensive restructuring.

"We expect Swiss bank stock prices to follow the example of the Anglo-Saxon banks, which have already largely completed their restructuring, and outperform," Bank Julius Baer's research head Hans Kaufmann said in a sector study.

Kaufmann and other analysts said sharp losses on Monday in UBS and CS Holding shares were a one-off reaction to weekend news that both banks were keeping large stakes in Swiss utilities rather than selling them, as had been speculated.
CS Holding fell 2.9 percent on Monday but regained 2.6 (corrects from 2.5) percent to close on Tuesday at 138.25 Swiss francs.
UBS opened 0.5 percent firmer after dropping 2.7 percent on Monday but eased in profit taking to close 0.4 percent ahead at 1,199 Swiss francs.
Beyond the utilities shock, analysts said a round of staff cuts, corporate reorganisation and one-time provisions to cover bad loans had boosted profit prospects from 1997 at UBS and SBC.

CS Holding was given similar good marks for adopting a new, leaner structure due to take effect on January 1 and slashing 3,500 Swiss jobs plus 1,500 worldwide, although it has not set aside exceptional provisions to cope with bad domestic loans.
All three banks face similar problems at home -- oversupply of retail banking in the small Swiss market and mounting loan risks after six years of slow growth in the Swiss economy.
These factors have cut down profit growth from some retail activities and from booming global business in asset management and investment banking.
"I think the restructuring steps have shown that, by European standards, the big Swiss banks are being very flexible and are addressing the problems," said John Leonard at Salomon Brothers in London.
Leonard said he was waiting to see how actual performance develops next year before revising his recommendations, which are now a buy for SBC and a hold for the other two.

SBC started the restructuring round in May by announcing a global reorganisation into four divisions, then in September said it would take an extraordinary loss of 1.9 billion Swiss francs ($1.4 billion) this year to pay for trimming Swiss operations and cutting loan risk.
CS Holding in July joined the trend by announcing its leaner structure as the renamed Credit Suisse Group, including a merger of separate domestic banks and a payroll cut of 15 percent.

UBS last week announced a three billion Swiss franc one-time charge to cover bad loans, resulting in a 1996 loss of around 500 million, plus a 3.7 percent cut in Swiss staff and a reduction in Swiss branches and regional divisions.
"I think the one-time provisions should be sufficient to cover loan risks," Pictet & Cie analyst Claudia von Tuerk said.
She noted that CS Holding has not taken a special charge for loans but that the bank group says it has kept exposure down by taking higher ordinary provisions.
Von Tuerk also said her recommendations were unchanged after dropping UBS from accumulate to hold after its three billion franc charge. She has CS as accumulate and SBC as a hold.
"We have had all the promises and the programs. Now we have to watch next year's performance to see whether they are actually doing what they said they would," she said. ($1=1.3260 Swiss Franc)
